edges.description: Estrogen-driven proliferation increases risk of hyperplasia and malignant progression.
Proliferative precursor epithelium provides a substrate for somatic driver selection.
Somatic pathway lesions support malignant outgrowth of endometrioid gland-forming epithelium.
Aberrant beta-catenin signaling contributes to malignant endometrioid epithelial behavior.
Hypermutated tumors create immunotherapy-relevant tumor antigenicity.
High mutational burden can create immunogenic tumor features.

Tamoxifen antagonises the oestrogen receptor in breast tissue while acting as a partial agonist at the endometrial receptor, so adjuvant therapy drives this node without progestin opposition. Local progestin delivery largely prevents the resulting endometrial pathology, which supports an opposable oestrogenic route rather than a separate genotoxic drug effect.

nodes.description: Hypermutated MMRd/MSI-H and POLE-mutated tumors are clinically important immunotherapy-sensitive contexts in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.

evidence.reference_title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Advanced Endometrial Cancer.
evidence.snippet: In patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer, the addition of pembrolizumab to standard chemotherapy resulted in significantly longer progression-free survival than with chemotherapy alone.

nodes.description: Progesterone deficiency and sustained estrogen-driven epithelial expansion can produce endometrial hyperplasia, which is a precursor context for endometrioid carcinoma.

evidence.reference_title: Understanding obesity and endometrial cancer risk: opportunities for prevention.
evidence.snippet: Conditions that are accompanied by prolonged progesterone deficiencies therefore promote endometrial proliferation and increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and its progression to endometrial cancer

nodes.description: Adjuvant tamoxifen for oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer raises endometrial carcinoma risk, and endometrioid histology predominates among the resulting tumours. The same exposure produces benign endometrial polyps, hyperplasia and increased sonographic thickness, so most endometrial change detected during tamoxifen therapy is not neoplastic.

nodes.description: Hyperestrogenic states promote mitogenic estrogen receptor signaling in endometrial glandular epithelium when progesterone counter-regulation is insufficient, increasing the proliferative substrate for endometrioid malignant transformation.

evidence.reference_title: Obesity, endogenous hormones, and endometrial cancer risk: a synthetic review.
evidence.snippet: endometrial cancer may develop as a result of the mitogenic effects of estrogens, when these are insufficiently counterbalanced by progesterone.
